solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Fast food outlet, principally cool and trendy in the 1960s

indicators.note: principally means chiefly or at the head, so only the opening letter of the word cool is taken

parts.note: a hippy was the fashionable flower-power type of the sixties

explanation.surface: A nostalgic look back at a fish-and-chip shop that was the height of cool in the swinging sixties.
explanation.walkthrough: CHIPPY is British slang for a fish-and-chip shop.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal British name for a takeaway selling fried fish and chips, a classic fast food outlet.

clue.text: Army unit American military leader put up in apartment block

indicators.note: in says the reversed letters are placed inside the apartment block word

parts.note: a condo is the American word for an apartment building

indicators.note: in a down clue, put up means the letters are read upwards, i.e. backwards
leader means the front letter of the word military

explanation.surface: A US general is billeted in a block of flats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put up' reads upwards in a down clue, turning the American abbreviation and military's first letter into MMA; condo is the American term for a block of flats.
explanation.definitionFit: A commando is a small military unit trained for raids, so it is an army unit.

clue.text: Insinuates naughty child is deceitful

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous child
someone who is deceitful lies

explanation.surface: Someone hints that a badly behaved youngster is a liar.
explanation.definitionFit: To insinuate something is to suggest it indirectly, which is a synonym for this verb.

clue.text: Singing star shops around to get very cheap diamonds?

indicators.note: around signals the letters of shops are turned about into a new order

parts.note: costing a penny, abbreviated P, is very cheap
ice is slang for diamonds

explanation.surface: A celebrity singer browses the shops looking for bargain diamonds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' is the anagram signal; something priced at a penny (P) is very cheap, and ice is slang for diamonds.
explanation.definitionFit: Victoria Beckham's nickname in the Spice Girls pop group, so she is a singing star.

clue.text: Old sailing vessel beginning to founder — I perish, sadly

indicators.note: beginning to means the opening letter of the word founder
sadly suggests things have gone wrong, so the letters of I perish are rearranged

explanation.surface: A sailor on a sinking ship laments his fate as it starts to go under.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sadly' rearranges I PERISH into IRESHIP, after F from 'beginning to founder'.
explanation.definitionFit: A vessel loaded with combustibles and set alight to drift among enemy ships in old naval warfare.

clue.text: Cricket fan perhaps incites rioting — over's ruined

indicators.note: rioting suggests disorder, so the letters of incites are scrambled
ruined means wrecked, so the letters of over are rearranged

parts.note: the 's is a link (over is), giving just the word over

explanation.surface: A cricket supporter stirs up a riot when an over is spoiled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rioting' turns INCITES into INSECTI and 'ruined' turns OVER into VORE. The cricket here is the insect, not the sport.
explanation.definitionFit: An animal that eats insects; one that likes eating crickets is an example, hence perhaps.

clue.text: What one needs to know about oriental verse form

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the slang word for information is written backwards

parts.note: dope is slang for the inside information you need
E for East, so oriental

explanation.surface: A question about what is needed to understand Eastern poetry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reverses DOPE to EPOD.
explanation.definitionFit: A lyric poem of alternating long and short lines, or the third part of a Greek ode, so a verse form.

clue.text: Mate holding computer connection?

indicators.note: holding means gripping around, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a hand is a fellow worker or mate
USB is the standard plug-in port on a computer

explanation.surface: A spouse is caught clutching a computer cable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mate' does double duty: it is the definition and, as hand (a fellow worker), the outer piece that 'holding' wraps round the plug-in port.
explanation.definitionFit: A husband is a woman's spouse, a partner or mate in marriage.

clue.text: Study gymnast's tricky manoeuvre?

parts.note: PE (physical education) is the gymnast's school subject
a ruse is a crafty trick

explanation.surface: A query about whether a gymnast's difficult move is worth studying.
explanation.walkthrough: PE stands for physical education, the school subject that includes gymnastics.
explanation.definitionFit: To peruse a text is to read or examine it carefully, a synonym of study.

clue.text: Listless male is taking heroin after work

parts.note: op, short for opus, is a musical work
H is slang for heroin

explanation.surface: A lethargic man has started using heroin after his shift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking' and 'after' simply join the pieces in order.
explanation.definitionFit: Mopish means gloomy and lacking energy, like someone moping, so listless.

clue.text: Being the marrying kind once, clairvoyant maybe accepts love

indicators.note: accepts means takes in, so the zero letter goes inside the other piece

parts.note: a clairvoyant might be a user of ESP, extrasensory perception
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A fortune-teller who welcomes romance used to be the type to wed.
explanation.walkthrough: ESP is extrasensory perception, so an ESP USER may be a clairvoyant.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic word for one who marries or takes a spouse, a being of the wedding kind in former times.

clue.text: A teacher can be wrong

parts.note: Miss is how pupils address a female teacher

explanation.surface: A teacher is capable of making mistakes.
explanation.definitionFit: Something amiss is faulty or not right, so it means wrong.

clue.text: Tests cakes mom baked with unknown ingredient

indicators.note: an ingredient goes into the mix, so the letter is put inside the scrambled letters
baked means mixed and cooked, so the letters of cakes mom are rearranged

parts.note: X is the classic unknown quantity in algebra

explanation.surface: Mother's cakes are tried out with a secret extra ingredient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'baked' rearranges CAKES MOM and 'ingredient' places X inside the result.
explanation.definitionFit: Practice examinations sat before the real ones are trial tests in British schools.

clue.text: Commanding soldiers to wear khaki?

indicators.note: to wear means to be clothed in, so the soldiers go inside the cloth

parts.note: khaki is a fabric, an example of material
GIs are American soldiers

explanation.surface: An authoritative order for troops to dress in khaki.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to wear' signals the soldiers going inside the cloth; khaki is a fabric, not just a colour, here.
explanation.definitionFit: Magisterial means authoritative and masterful in manner, as a commanding presence is.

clue.text: Recognised noble

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both eminent and acclaimed, and dignified or aristocratic in appearance.

clue.text: Top-selling numbers of Punch and American magazine

parts.note: to punch someone is to hit them
Parade is a US Sunday newspaper magazine

explanation.surface: Bestselling issues of the British humour magazine Punch and a US weekly.
explanation.walkthrough: Punch was a long-running British satirical magazine, which makes it look like a title rather than a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A chart of the best-selling records, with numbers meaning songs.

clue.text: Ex-cricketer's nasty threat to cricket side

indicators.note: nasty suggests something twisted, so the letters of threat are reordered

parts.note: the on side is the leg side of a cricket field

explanation.surface: A former player makes an unpleasant threat to an opposing team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nasty' rearranges THREAT into ATHERT. Mike Atherton is a former England cricket captain; the 's is just 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Michael Atherton captained England at cricket in the 1990s, so he is a former player.

clue.text: He comes in to eat scones, freshly prepared for a quick snack?

indicators.note: comes in means enters, so the pronoun goes inside the reworked letters
freshly prepared suggests the letters of to eat scones are made anew in another order

explanation.surface: A man arrives to tuck into newly baked scones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'freshly prepared' rearranges TO EAT SCONES and 'comes in' puts HE inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Melted cheddar on grilled bread is a classic fast light bite, hence a quick snack.

clue.text: Big guns announced decrees

indicators.note: announced means spoken out, so the word for decrees is heard rather than written

parts.note: canons are church laws or decrees

explanation.surface: Heavy artillery and official edicts are proclaimed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'announced' says CANONS, which sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Cannons are large artillery pieces, literally big guns.

clue.text: Bother to squeeze letter in marginal note

indicators.note: to squeeze means to hold tight, so the mail goes inside the trouble word

parts.note: to ail someone is to trouble or bother them
post means mail, i.e. letters

explanation.surface: Someone takes the trouble to cram a letter into a note in the margin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to squeeze' signals the insertion; 'Bother' is a verb, meaning to trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: An apostil is an annotation written in the margin of a text, a rare word for a marginal gloss.

clue.text: Money added to bill, in a manner of speaking

indicators.note: added to means the money word is placed after the bill word

parts.note: AC is short for account, a bill
a cent is a coin, a unit of money

explanation.surface: A surcharge has been put on the bill, so to speak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a manner of speaking' looks like a throwaway phrase but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An accent is a distinctive way of pronouncing words, a style of speech.

clue.text: Specialised vocabulary one's associated with English language

parts.note: cant is jargon peculiar to a group
taken as written, without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Technical jargon belongs to the English tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: Cantonese is a Chinese tongue spoken in Hong Kong and Guangdong, so a language.

clue.text: Important figure turning up in Alabama borough?

indicators.note: turning up says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A notable person makes an appearance in a town in Alabama.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'turning up' reads upwards: AMABO, found in AlabAMA BOrough, read backwards. The in of 'in Alabama' marks the letters as sitting inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Barack Obama, a US president, is an example of an important figure, hence the question mark.

clue.text: In Lincoln, find empty old house

indicators.note: In says the emptied word sits inside the president's name

parts.note: Abe is the nickname of Abraham Lincoln

indicators.note: empty means the middle is removed, leaving only the outside letters

explanation.surface: A visit to Lincoln to locate a derelict ancient house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'empty' cuts OLD to OD. Lincoln looks like the English city but is Abraham Lincoln.
explanation.definitionFit: An abode is a home or dwelling, so a house.

clue.text: Say Middle Eastern inhabitant has a self-centred obsession

parts.note: e.g. (for example) is signalled by say
an Omani lives in Oman, in the Middle East

explanation.surface: Someone from the Gulf is said to be obsessed with himself.
explanation.definitionFit: An extreme preoccupation with oneself and one's importance, a self-absorbed fixation.

clue.text: Too old to have drink in pint container

indicators.note: in places the wine inside the abbreviation for pint

parts.note: Asti is a sparkling Italian wine

explanation.surface: Someone is too old to drink from a pint glass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'container' simply makes the surface read: the pint holds the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom for someone no longer capable through age, past their best.

clue.text: Like pupils taking 12 Across, fixed after half term

indicators.note: after means the steady word follows the half word
half means the first two of the four letters of term

parts.note: fixed means firm and steady

explanation.surface: Students sitting practice exams after a half-term break.
explanation.walkthrough: 12 Across is MOCK EXAMS, so the pupils are examinable.
explanation.definitionFit: Pupils sitting trial exams can be examined, which is a synonym for this adjective.

clue.text: Film director nearly collapsed

indicators.note: nearly means not quite complete, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: Federico Fellini was an Italian film director

explanation.surface: A film-maker very nearly fell down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nearly' drops the final I from FELLINI.
explanation.definitionFit: Phrasal verb for caving in, as a roof does when it collapses.
